mutants.description: The soft-start trip line is copied from the run-trip line and widens the soft-start count from the run-count width (FCNT_RUN_W), so a full 32-cycle soft-start count loses its top bit and reads as 0.
mutants.reason: When trip_ss is 32 (the highest value reg_file allows), a completely faulted soft-start window gives a count of 32 that compares as 0, so window_trip_SS never asserts. With a lower trip_ss, window_trip_SS drops again when the count reaches 32.

mutants.description: The soft-start trip is checked only on the cycle-boundary strobe pwm_rise, as if it were sampled together with the window, instead of following the soft-start count all the time.
mutants.reason: In S_SS with the count at or above trip_ss, window_trip_SS pulses for one clock at each PWM rising edge instead of staying high. It also reacts at the next edge, not at once, when trip_ss is lowered.

mutants.description: The soft-start window is rewritten to put the new sample in at the MSB and shift right, but the count still subtracts bit WINDOW_SS-1 as the leaving bit, and that bit is now the newest sample.
mutants.reason: In S_SS each faulted cycle is taken off again on the next pwm_rise, so fault_count_ss never builds above about 1 under a sustained overcurrent. window_trip_SS never fires for trip_ss >= 2, and the soft-start telemetry is wrong.

mutants.description: The bit leaving the run window is copied across the whole count width instead of zero-extended, so a faulted cycle that leaves the 16-cycle run window adds one to fault_count_run instead of taking one off.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN, once a faulted cycle is older than 16 cycles, fault_count_run goes up instead of down. fault_count_run_out goes above the real number of faulted cycles, and window_trip can assert, or stay asserted, after the overcurrent has ended.

mutants.description: The idle clear resets the two shift registers but leaves both counts holding their values from before the hiccup.
mutants.reason: After a window trip and hiccup, the run count keeps its old value, for example trip_run. Because the cleared window has no faulted bits left to take off, window_trip asserts as soon as S_RUN is entered again. In the same way, the soft-start count makes window_trip_SS fire on re-entry to S_SS, and both telemetry counts stay non-zero in idle.

mutants.description: The sample entering the soft-start window is copied across the count width instead of zero-extended, so a faulted cycle entering the window adds all-ones (-1) to fault_count_ss instead of +1.
mutants.reason: In S_SS a faulted cycle makes fault_count_ss go down, wrapping below zero to large values. window_trip_SS then asserts on the first faulted cycle when the count wraps to 63 from 0, and fault_count_ss_out reports nonsense.

mutants.description: The new run-window sample is copied across the whole run shift register instead of being zero-extended into bit 0, so one faulted cycle marks every slot of the run window as faulted.
mutants.reason: In S_RUN, a single faulted cycle followed by clean cycles fills the window with ones, so fault_count_run goes down by one for each of the next 16 cycles even though it was only raised once. The count wraps and goes wrong, which changes fault_count_run_out and window_trip.
